title: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
contentObjective: I can write and interpret percents greater than 100% and less than 1%.
languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words percent, greater than 100%, less than 1%, and equivalent.

noticeAndWonder.context: The arcade leaderboard shows one player scored 150% of the weekly goal, while a rare bonus round only adds a 0.5% point boost. How can a score be more than the whole goal, and how tiny is a 0.5% boost?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Power-Up Boost
revealWordProblem.text: In the arcade game, your base score is 80 points. A rare power-up boosts your score to 250% of your base. How many points do you have after the power-up? (Hint: 250% means 2.5 times the base.)
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 250% = 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5, so 2.5 × 80 = 200 points. Because 250% is greater than 100%, the new score (200) is more than the base score (80).

turnAndTalk.question: The leaderboard shows one player hit 150% of the goal and a bonus round gives a 0.5% boost. How can a percent be more than the whole, and how can one be a tiny sliver?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 150% is more than one whole, and 0.5% is a tiny piece smaller than 1%.

vocabulary.term: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%

vocabulary.definition: Percents can describe amounts greater than one whole or smaller than one hundredth of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los porcentajes pueden describir cantidades mayores que un entero o menores que una centésima de un entero.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A number out of 100, written with a % sign, is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: A percent bigger than 100%, more than the whole thing.

vocabulary.definition: A percent smaller than 1%, a very tiny part.

conceptIntro.heading: How can a percent be more than the whole, or smaller than a tiny piece?
conceptIntro.intro: 100% means one whole. A percent greater than 100% is more than the whole. A percent less than 1% is a very tiny part.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To change any percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left).

optional.correctWork: 0.5% does NOT equal 0.5. To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal two places left): 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005. So 0.5% = 0.005, a tiny boost far less than 1% — not a huge 50% boost.

optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — el impulso que desaparece

optional.explanationEs: El error está en el paso que solo quita el signo de porcentaje: borrar el % no convierte nada. Pasar de porcentaje a decimal significa dividir entre 100, así que 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005, un impulso mucho menor que 1%, no el 50% (la mitad de los puntos) que dijo el estudiante.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: Since 120% has three digits, the student writes 12.0 instead of dividing by 100.

approaching.correctWork: 120% means 120 out of 100. Divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left): 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2. So 120% = 1.2, which makes sense because it is only a little more than one whole (100%).
hints: Dividing by 100 always moves the decimal point two places to the left, no matter how many digits the percent has.
1.2 is only slightly more than 1 whole, matching 120% being only slightly more than 100%. 12.0 would mean 1,200% — way too big.
approaching.explanation: In the Attempt step the student counted digits instead of dividing by 100, which shifted the decimal only one place. Because 120% means 120 out of 100, the decimal is 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2 — just a little more than one whole, which fits a percent just above 100%.
approaching.explanationEs: En el paso del intento, el estudiante contó dígitos en lugar de dividir entre 100, y así movió el punto decimal solo un lugar. Como 120% significa 120 de cada 100, el decimal es 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2, un poco más de un entero, lo cual coincide con un porcentaje apenas mayor que 100%.

onLevel.instructions: Match each value to its equivalent percent.

Start with 1.5: slide the decimal two places right to get its percent. Then 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 tells you which card 3/2 pairs with.
onLevel.explanation: Every pair uses the same move: multiply the decimal by 100 to get the percent. That makes 1.5 = 150%, 2.75 = 275%, 0.003 = 0.3%, and 0.008 = 0.8%, while the fractions become decimals first — 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 = 150% and 1 ÷ 200 = 0.005 = 0.5%.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada pareja usa el mismo movimiento: multiplicar el decimal por 100 para obtener el porcentaje. Así 1.5 = 150%, 2.75 = 275%, 0.003 = 0.3% y 0.008 = 0.8%, mientras que las fracciones primero se convierten en decimales: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 = 150% y 1 ÷ 200 = 0.005 = 0.5%.

onLevel.explanationEs: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004. Mueve el punto decimal dos lugares a la izquierda.
hintsEs: 0.4% es menos que 1%, así que el decimal correspondiente debe ser menor que 0.01.
Divide el porcentaje entre 100: el punto decimal se mueve dos lugares a la izquierda y los ceros llenan los huecos.
Empieza en 0.4 y salta el punto dos veces a la izquierda: 0.4 → 0.04 → un salto más da la forma de la respuesta.

onLevel.instructions: Convert each percent to a decimal and a fraction.
hints: The finished row shows the pattern: 150% → 1.5 → 3/2. Percents over 100% give decimals over 1; tiny percents give tiny decimals.
Percent → decimal: divide by 100. Decimal → fraction: write it over a power of 10 (or over 200, 400) and simplify.
Row 2: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 for the decimal. Then write 2.5 as 25/10 and simplify. Use the same steps for 0.5% and 0.25%.
onLevel.explanation: Each percent is divided by 100 for the decimal, then written as a fraction: 250% → 2.5 → 5/2, 0.5% → 0.005 → 1/200, and 0.25% → 0.0025 → 1/400. Percents above 100% land above 1 on the decimal side, while percents below 1% land below 0.01.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada porcentaje se divide entre 100 para obtener el decimal y luego se escribe como fracción: 250% → 2.5 → 5/2, 0.5% → 0.005 → 1/200 y 0.25% → 0.0025 → 1/400. Los porcentajes mayores que 100% quedan por encima de 1 en el decimal, mientras que los menores que 1% quedan por debajo de 0.01.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Convierte cada porcentaje a decimal y a fracción.
hintsEs: La fila terminada muestra el patrón: 150% → 1.5 → 3/2. Los porcentajes mayores de 100% dan decimales mayores que 1; los porcentajes diminutos dan decimales diminutos.
Porcentaje → decimal: divide entre 100. Decimal → fracción: escríbelo sobre una potencia de 10 (o sobre 200, 400) y simplifica.
Fila 2: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 para el decimal. Luego escribe 2.5 como 25/10 y simplifica. Usa los mismos pasos con 0.5% y 0.25%.

onLevel.label: Place these percents on a number line from 0 to 3: A = 50%, B = 150%, C = 275%
hints: This number line runs 0 to 3, so percents above 100% will land past the 1 mark.
Convert each percent to a decimal (divide by 100), then place that decimal on the line.
A: 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5, so A sits halfway between 0 and 1. Convert B and C the same way before placing them.
onLevel.explanation: Dividing each percent by 100 gives its position: A = 50% = 0.5 sits halfway between 0 and 1, B = 150% = 1.5 sits halfway between 1 and 2, and C = 275% = 2.75 sits three quarters of the way from 2 to 3. Anything past the 1 mark is a percent greater than 100%.
onLevel.explanationEs: Dividir cada porcentaje entre 100 da su posición: A = 50% = 0.5 queda a la mitad entre 0 y 1, B = 150% = 1.5 queda a la mitad entre 1 y 2, y C = 275% = 2.75 queda a tres cuartos del camino de 2 a 3. Todo lo que pasa la marca del 1 es un porcentaje mayor que 100%.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A rare item has a 0.8% drop chance. Write 0.8% as a decimal.

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: The student divides 0.8 by 10 instead of 100, moving the decimal only one place.

onLevel.correctWork: To change a percent to a decimal, always divide by 100 — move the decimal point TWO places to the left, not one. 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008. So 0.8% = 0.008, which is far less than 1% (0.01), matching the tiny drop chance in the problem.
hints: Dividing by 100 moves the decimal two places, not one — dividing by 10 is a different operation.
0.08 would actually mean 8%, which is much bigger than the tiny 0.8% drop chance described in the problem.
onLevel.explanation: In the Attempt step the student divided by 10 and moved the decimal only one place. Percent to decimal always means dividing by 100, so 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008 — a value below 0.01, which matches a drop chance smaller than 1%.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso del intento, el estudiante dividió entre 10 y movió el punto decimal solo un lugar. Pasar de porcentaje a decimal siempre significa dividir entre 100, así que 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008, un valor menor que 0.01, que coincide con una probabilidad de aparición menor que 1%.

extending.title: Find the Percent Error

workedExample.label: Move the decimal two places left

extending.correctWork: 0.6% means 0.6 out of 100. Move the decimal two places left: 0.6 → 0.006. The correct answer is 0.6% = 0.006.
hints: The student only moved the decimal one place instead of two.
0.6% is less than 1%, so the decimal must be less than 0.01. 0.06 is too large.
extending.explanation: The step that moves the decimal shifted 0.6 only one place, landing on 0.06 instead of 0.006. Since 0.6% means 0.6 out of 100, the decimal point moves two places left, and the result must be below 0.01 because 0.6% is less than 1%.
extending.explanationEs: El paso que mueve el punto decimal movió 0.6 solo un lugar y llegó a 0.06 en vez de 0.006. Como 0.6% significa 0.6 de cada 100, el punto decimal se mueve dos lugares a la izquierda, y el resultado debe ser menor que 0.01 porque 0.6% es menor que 1%.

extending.prompt: A game character has 300% of its original health after picking up a power-up. If the original health was 80 points, how many health points does the character have now? A student says 240 points. Another says 380 points. Who is correct and why?
extending.sentenceFrame: The student who said ___ is correct because 300% means ___ times the original, so ___ × 80 = ___.
extending.hint: If the character has 300% health after the power-up, think: what does 300% mean compared to 100%?
hints: 300% is three whole 100%'s — the health got MORE than the original, not less.
Convert 300% to a decimal (divide by 100), then multiply that decimal by the original 80 points.
Write 300% as 300 ÷ 100 = 3.0. Multiply 3.0 × 80 and compare your result with each student's claim.
extending.explanation: The student who said 240 points is correct. 300% means three whole 100%'s, so it is 300 ÷ 100 = 3 times the original: 3 × 80 = 240 points. The answer 380 comes from adding 300 to 80, which treats the percent like a plain number instead of a multiplier.
extending.explanationEs: El estudiante que dijo 240 puntos tiene razón. 300% significa tres veces el 100% completo, así que es 300 ÷ 100 = 3 veces lo original: 3 × 80 = 240 puntos. La respuesta de 380 viene de sumar 300 a 80, lo que trata el porcentaje como un número común en lugar de un multiplicador.

extending.instructions: A bacteria population starts at 500. Complete the table showing what each percent of the original population equals.
hints: The finished row shows the recipe: turn the percent into a decimal, then multiply by 500.
Percent → decimal (divide by 100), then decimal × 500 = number of bacteria.
For 175%: write 175 ÷ 100 = 1.75, so the calculation is 1.75 × 500. Do 0.5% and 300% the same way.
extending.explanation: Each row turns the percent into a decimal and multiplies by the starting 500: 175% → 1.75 × 500 = 875, 0.5% → 0.005 × 500 = 2.5, and 300% → 3.0 × 500 = 1500. Percents above 100% give more than the original 500, while 0.5% gives only a tiny sliver of it.
extending.explanationEs: Cada fila convierte el porcentaje en decimal y lo multiplica por las 500 bacterias iniciales: 175% → 1.75 × 500 = 875, 0.5% → 0.005 × 500 = 2.5 y 300% → 3.0 × 500 = 1500. Los porcentajes mayores que 100% dan más que las 500 originales, mientras que 0.5% da apenas una pequeñísima parte.
extending.instructionsEs: Una población de bacterias empieza en 500. Completa la tabla mostrando a cuánto equivale cada porcentaje de la población original.
hintsEs: La fila terminada muestra la receta: convierte el porcentaje en decimal y luego multiplica por 500.
Porcentaje → decimal (divide entre 100) y luego decimal × 500 = número de bacterias.
Para 175%: escribe 175 ÷ 100 = 1.75, así que el cálculo es 1.75 × 500. Haz 0.5% y 300% igual.

optionalActivity.name: Extreme Percent Sort
optionalActivity.intro: The arcade's leaderboard is full of wild percents — sort the tiny boosts from the giant jackpots, then figure out what each one really means!

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1% is treating every percent-to-decimal conversion the same way regardless of size — for example, writing 150% as 0.15 (as if it were an ordinary under-100% percent) instead of 1.5, or writing 0.5% as 0.5 (forgetting to divide by 100 at all) instead of 0.005. Before finalizing an answer, check that the decimal for any percent over 100% is greater than 1, and the decimal for any percent under 1% is less than 0.01.

diagram.title: 300% Jackpot of 30 Tokens
diagram.caption: The top bar is your 30 tokens (100% = one whole); the jackpot bar stacks three 30-token wholes, so 300% = 90 tokens — more than what you put in.

choiceFeedback: 0.25% is less than 1%, so it's a very small amount.
As a decimal, 0.25% is very tiny — convert carefully.
As a fraction, 0.25% is one quarter of one percent.
hints: Careful: 0.25% is NOT the same as 0.25. The % sign means it still needs to be divided by 100.
Convert 0.25% to a decimal first (divide by 100), then test each statement against that decimal.
Start at 0.25 and slide the decimal two places left: 0.25 → 0.025 → one more hop. Now check which statement matches.
